title: Open WebUI chat listener -- T1059 non-same-origin postMessage triggers submitPrompt() in victim session
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54007 (GHSA-3vv5-8xxp-4f55,
CVSS 7.1 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

Open WebUI's chat message listener accepted `input:prompt` and
`action:submit` `postMessage` events regardless of the sending
window's origin -- no same-origin check. An external, ATTACKER-CONTROLLED
web page can therefore set arbitrary prompt text and trigger
`submitPrompt()` inside an authenticated victim's Open WebUI tab simply
by having the victim visit the attacker's page while logged in
elsewhere. The advisory's own validation: a cross-origin attacker page
that auto-posts these messages causes unauthorized
`POST /api/v1/chats/new` and `POST /api/chat/completions` requests
carrying attacker-controlled prompt content -- cross-site forced model/
tool execution under the victim's own privileges, entirely without
their consent or awareness.

Detection logic flags a `POST /api/chat/completions` or
`POST /api/v1/chats/new` request whose Referer/Origin header is ABSENT
or does not match the Open WebUI deployment's own origin, combined with
timing consistent with a `postMessage`-triggered auto-submission rather
than direct user interaction -- since the vulnerable listener has no
origin gate, any successful cross-origin trigger reaches these
endpoints as if it were a same-origin request.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, describing the researcher's own cross-origin
attacker-page validation), fixed in 0.9.6.
